context: An elderly couple reminisces about company dinners of old
purpose: Teach: 丼/宴会/唇/食物/爪/昨晩/汚い/症候群

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昨晩テレビで昔の宴会の特集をやっていてな、つい見入ってしまったよ。
lines.en: Last night on TV there was a special about old-style company banquets, and I just got drawn in watching it.
lines.style: Nostalgic, slow opener with a wistful smile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: あら、懐かしいわね。あなたの会社の宴会、いつも牛丼屋の二階だったでしょう。
lines.en: Oh my, how nostalgic. Your company's banquets were always on the second floor of that beef bowl shop, weren't they.
lines.style: Warm and teasing with affectionate laughter underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうそう、課長が真っ赤な唇で熱燗を飲み干して、皆で大笑いしたもんだ。
lines.en: Yes, yes — the section chief would drain his hot sake with bright red lips, and everyone would burst out laughing.
lines.style: Animated reminiscing, chuckling between phrases warmly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: テーブルが食物の残りで汚いままで、誰も片付けなかったって嘆いていたわよね。
lines.en: You used to complain that the tables stayed dirty with leftover food and nobody ever cleared them.
lines.style: Gentle ribbing, raising her eyebrows knowingly at him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今思えば、あれも一種の昭和症候群みたいなもんだな。仕事の延長で飲み続けるという。
lines.en: Looking back now, it was a kind of Showa-era syndrome, wasn't it — drinking on and on as an extension of work.
lines.style: Reflective, slightly self-deprecating with a soft sigh.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: あなた帰ってきて、爪の間まで煙草の匂いがしみついていたのを覚えてるわ。
lines.en: I still remember how, when you came home, the smell of cigarettes had soaked in even under your fingernails.
lines.style: Soft, almost fond memory shared quietly together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: すまなかったな。今度の日曜は、二人で静かに親子丼でも食べに行こうか。
lines.en: I'm sorry about that. This coming Sunday, why don't the two of us go out quietly for some oyakodon together.
lines.style: Sincere apology, soft and tender invitation extended.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: いいわね。歳をとって、やっと静かな食事のありがたみがわかるなんてね。
lines.en: That sounds lovely. To think it took growing old before we finally understood the value of a quiet meal.
lines.style: Contented, lightly laughing with grateful warmth showing.
